name: SatNOGS DB RF Transmitter Source Nodes
description: SatNOGS DB (Libre Space Foundation) -> SDS $RFB transmitter records (typed contracts 1.0: FlatBuffers only, no JSON and no base64 between modules). Two pure flow nodes: `request` turns a TimerTick into ONE whole-table HttpRequest (HREQ) GET of https://db.satnogs.org/api/transmitters/?format=json (bulk, never a pagination walk — the source-policy.json crawl ruling) whose CONTEXT is the parse job, one size-prefixed IngestRequest (INGQ) skeleton (schema, provider, source name and URL, reconcile None, archive naming), echoed by hostcap/http-request in the HttpResponse; `parse` reads that HttpResponse (HRSP), decodes ~4,994 transmitter rows and emits a size-prefixed $RFB record stream, the IngestRequest for hostcap/storage-ingest (the job completed with the batch id, licence tags and provenance) and the HttpResponse verbatim as the raw document. One $RFB record carries exactly one LINK_DIRECTION, so a Transceiver/Transponder becomes an UPLINK + DOWNLINK pair sharing ID_TRANSMITTER (the SatNOGS uuid). SatNOGS publishes HERTZ; every frequency field written is MHz per the normative RFB units rule. Licence is CC-BY-SA-4.0: every record carries CITATION verbatim and the batch's source tags carry LICENSE CC-BY-SA-4.0, LICENSE_URL, CITATION and SHARE_ALIKE true so the share-alike obligation survives republication. Node CONFIG through the builtin plugin.getConfig hostcall (SDS $PIV, one ModuleConfig FlatBuffer): satnogs_transmitters_url, satnogs_http_timeout_ms, satnogs_provider_id, satnogs_if_none_match, satnogs_if_modified_since, satnogs_record_cap. No capabilities: this node performs no I/O — http and storage are the generic hostcap connector nodes. HTTP 304 Not Modified is accepted, never treated as a failed fetch: the parse method emits a single FlowNotice (Unchanged, not-modified) on its 'unchanged' port and nothing else, so no batch is stored or announced.

sequentialJustification.detail: Both methods are pure single-pass transforms over one fetched JSON table: `request` builds one HttpRequest from node CONFIG, and `parse` walks the SatNOGS transmitter rows once, emitting one or two $RFB records per row into a single append-only stream. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool, no fan-out and nothing for a second thread to do; the whole cost is one linear scan of a ~3.5 MB body. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles clang/wasi-sequential rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: Builds the SatNOGS transmitters fetch from a TimerTick: ONE whole-table HttpRequest per cycle with the identifying User-Agent source-policy.json mandates, conditional-request validators from node CONFIG when set, and the parse job in CONTEXT (one size-prefixed IngestRequest). BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is now refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames.

acceptedTypeSets.description: TimerTick (module-sdk runtime type TICK) from the flow's timer trigger.

inputPorts.description: Cron timer tick (its fields are not read).

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpRequest (HREQ) for hostcap/http-request: GET the transmitters table, headers user-agent / accept (and if-none-match / if-modified-since from CONFIG), TIMEOUT_MS satnogs_http_timeout_ms; CONTEXT: the parse job, one size-prefixed IngestRequest (SCHEMA RFB.fbs, TAGS PROVIDER_ID / SOURCE_NAME satnogs-db / SOURCE_URL, RECONCILE None, ARCHIVE satnogs / transmitters.json).

methods.description: Reads the HttpResponse carrying the SatNOGS transmitters table and its job (CONTEXT), decodes each transmitter row into one $RFB record per link direction (Hz -> MHz, explicit UNKNOWN polarization) and emits a size-prefixed $RFB record stream, the IngestRequest for storage-ingest and the HttpResponse verbatim for archiving. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is now refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames. HTTP 304 Not Modified is accepted, never treated as a failed fetch: the host presents the ETag / Last-Modified it recorded from the previous 2xx for this URL, so an unchanged table answers 304 with no body. The method then emits a single FlowNotice on its 'unchanged' port and nothing else, so no batch is stored or announced. Any other non-200 status (or a failed exchange, STATUS 0) fails closed with nothing emitted.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (HRSP) from hostcap/http-request: STATUS, HEADERS, BODY verbatim, the request's CONTEXT (the job, a size-prefixed IngestRequest), RETRIEVED_MS.

inputPorts.description: The HTTP response carrying the SatNOGS transmitters table, its job echoed in CONTEXT.

acceptedTypeSets.description: IngestRequest (INGQ) for hostcap/storage-ingest: SCHEMA RFB.fbs, TAGS (PROVIDER_ID, SOURCE_NAME, BATCH_ID = sha256 of the payload, SOURCE_URL, CONTENT_KEY_ID public, SOURCE_PEER source:satnogs, LICENSE CC-BY-SA-4.0, LICENSE_URL, CITATION, SHARE_ALIKE true), RECONCILE from the job (None), ARCHIVE from the job, PROVENANCE (status, validators, retrieval time, parser, source / normalized SHA-256, counts).
The HttpResponse (HRSP) the batch was made from, verbatim: its BODY is the SatNOGS transmitters JSON storage-ingest archives under the request's ARCHIVE naming.
FlowNotice (FNTC): KIND Unchanged, SCHEMA RFB.fbs, PROVIDER_ID, SOURCE_NAME, REASON not-modified, ITEMS the source URL, AT_MS the host's retrieval time.

outputPorts.description: Emitted ONLY when the fetch answered HTTP 304 Not Modified (the host sent the recorded ETag / Last-Modified validators): one notice frame and no meta/records/raw frames, so the ingest node never becomes ready and nothing is stored or announced.
